def-finite-conservative-production-destr:
## Definition

Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and a domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$; its admissible nonnegative states are $\Omega_+:=\Omega\cap[0,\infty)^m$. For every ordered pair $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $p_{ij},d_{ij}:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be production and destruction transfer rates that are nonnegative on $\Omega_+$. A **finite conservative production destruction system** (finite conservative PDS) is the autonomous ODE

$$y_i'=F_i(y):=\sum_{j=1}^m\bigl(p_{ij}(y)-d_{ij}(y)\bigr),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m,$$

with internal-transfer identities

$$p_{ij}(y)=d_{ji}(y),\qquad p_{ii}(y)=d_{ii}(y)=0.$$

The index $j$ is the donor/source of $p_{ij}$ and the index $i$ is its recipient/destination; $d_{ji}$ is the same transfer viewed as destruction from $j$. The total mass is $M(y):=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i$. The ODE is considered at states in $\Omega_+$. The definition describes a closed system: external sources and sinks must be specified separately and are not included in the conservation claims on this page. No existence, positivity, or regularity assertion about solutions is part of this definition.
lem-strict-column-dominance-implies-nonn:
## Statement

Let $M=(m_{ij})\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ for a finite $m\ge1$. Suppose $m_{jj}>0$, $m_{ij}\le0$ for $i\ne j$, and

$$m_{jj}>\sum_{i\ne j}|m_{ij}|\qquad(j=1,\ldots,m).$$

Then $M$ is invertible and every entry of $M^{-1}$ is nonnegative. If $b\in\mathbb R^m$ has nonnegative coordinates, then $M^{-1}b\ge0$; if every coordinate of $b$ is positive, then every coordinate of $M^{-1}b$ is positive.
alg-modified-patankar-euler:
## Definition

Let $m\ge1$, let $y^n\in[0,\infty)^m$, let $h>0$, and let $(p_{ij},d_{ij})$ be the rates of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]]. Choose declared denominators $\sigma_i>0$. The **modified Patankar Euler step** returns the unique solution $y^{n+1}$ of

$$y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+h\sum_{j\ne i}\left(p_{ij}(y^n)\frac{y_j^{n+1}}{\sigma_j}-d_{ij}(y^n)\frac{y_i^{n+1}}{\sigma_i}\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.$$

Equivalently, form $M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ by

$$M_{ii}=1+h\sum_{j\ne i}\frac{d_{ij}(y^n)}{\sigma_i},\qquad M_{ij}=-h\frac{p_{ij}(y^n)}{\sigma_j}\quad(i\ne j),$$

and solve $My^{n+1}=y^n$. The admissible conditions are exactly the finite conservative PDS identities, $y^n\ge0$, $h>0$, and $\sigma_i>0$. Return an inadmissible-input status if any condition fails; otherwise return the unique exact solution of the stated linear system. The standard first-order choice is $\sigma_i=y_i^n$, which is admissible only when every $y_i^n>0$. A separately defined rate-factor form extends a first-order step to zero donor coordinates under an additional source-factorization hypothesis.
def-source-factored-production-destructi:
## Definition

Let $(p_{ij},d_{ij})$ be the rates of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]]. A **source-factored transfer representation** on an open set $U\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ containing a compact set $K\subseteq[0,\infty)^m$ consists of functions $a_{ij}:U\to\mathbb R$, $i\ne j$, such that each $a_{ij}$ is $C^2$ on $U$ in the sense of [[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]], is nonnegative on $U\cap[0,\infty)^m$, and, for every $y\in U\cap[0,\infty)^m$,

$$p_{ij}(y)=y_j a_{ij}(y),\qquad d_{ij}(y)=y_i a_{ji}(y),\qquad a_{ii}:=0.$$

Here $a_{ij}$ is the transfer rate from donor $j$ to recipient $i$ per unit of donor quantity. Nonnegativity is required on admissible nonnegative states; the $C^2$ extension to the open neighborhood is used for local analysis and need not be nonnegative at inadmissible states with negative coordinates. The factorization is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of nonnegative rates and the identity $p_{ij}=d_{ji}$. On strictly positive states the ratio $p_{ij}(y)/y_j$ equals $a_{ij}(y)$; at a zero donor coordinate the factorized coefficient remains defined and avoids the indeterminate expression $0/0$.
alg-zero-compatible-modified-patankar-eu:
## Definition

Let $y^n\in K$ for a compact nonnegative state set $K$ with a source-factored transfer representation [[def-source-factored-production-destruction-rates]], and let $h>0$. Form $B(y^n)\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ by

$$B_{ij}(y^n)=a_{ij}(y^n)\ (i\ne j),\qquad B_{jj}(y^n)=-\sum_{i\ne j}a_{ij}(y^n).$$

Return the unique solution $y^{n+1}$ of

$$\bigl(I-hB(y^n)\bigr)y^{n+1}=y^n.$$

Equivalently, component $i$ satisfies

$$y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+h\sum_{j\ne i}\left(a_{ij}(y^n)y_j^{n+1}-a_{ji}(y^n)y_i^{n+1}\right).$$

This procedure uses no denominator $y_j^n$ and is defined when some donor coordinates vanish. It is the factorized extension of the first-order Patankar Euler formula to the zero-state boundary. In exact arithmetic its linear system is uniquely solvable by [[lem-strict-column-dominance-implies-nonnegative-inverse]].
alg-mprk22-1:
## Definition

Let $y^n\in(0,\infty)^m$, let $h>0$, and let $(p_{ij},d_{ij})$ be the rates of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]]. First compute the stage $z$ by invoking [[alg-modified-patankar-euler]] with denominators $\sigma_i=y_i^n$:

$$z_i=y_i^n+h\sum_{j\ne i}\left(p_{ij}(y^n)\frac{z_j}{y_j^n}-d_{ij}(y^n)\frac{z_i}{y_i^n}\right).$$

Then form $B(y^n,z)$ with, for $i\ne j$,

$$B_{ij}(y^n,z):=\frac{p_{ij}(y^n)+p_{ij}(z)}{2z_j},\qquad B_{jj}(y^n,z):=-\sum_{i\ne j}B_{ij}(y^n,z),$$

and solve

$$\bigl(I-hB(y^n,z)\bigr)y^{n+1}=y^n.$$

Equivalently,

$$y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+\frac h2\sum_{j\ne i}\left((p_{ij}(y^n)+p_{ij}(z))\frac{y_j^{n+1}}{z_j}-(d_{ij}(y^n)+d_{ij}(z))\frac{y_i^{n+1}}{z_i}\right).$$

Inputs with nonpositive $y_i^n$ or $h\le0$ are inadmissible. The algorithm returns stage-failure or update-failure if a required linear system is not uniquely solvable; under the stated conservative PDS and positive-input hypotheses, [[lem-strict-column-dominance-implies-nonnegative-inverse]] guarantees both solves are uniquely solvable and the stage is positive. No zero-stage or denominator-regularized second-order variant is defined here.
thm-modified-patankar-euler-positive-con:
## Statement

For a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]], an input $y^n\ge0$, step $h>0$, and any positive denominators $\sigma_i>0$, the step of [[alg-modified-patankar-euler]] is uniquely defined, satisfies $y^{n+1}\ge0$, and conserves total mass:

$$\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^{n+1}=\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^n.$$

If $y^n>0$ coordinatewise, then $y^{n+1}>0$ coordinatewise. These conclusions do not assert order for arbitrary denominators; the first-order choice and its accuracy hypotheses are treated separately.
lem-modified-patankar-euler-positive-tub:
## Statement

Let $F$ be the vector field of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]] on a bounded open convex set $U\subset\Omega\cap\mathbb R_{>0}^m$ with $\overline U\subset\mathbb R_{>0}^m$. Suppose the transfer rates are $C^2$ on an open neighborhood of $\overline U$, and their derivatives through order two are bounded there. For $y\in U$, let $\Phi_h(y)$ be [[alg-modified-patankar-euler]] with the standard denominators $\sigma_i=y_i$. Then there are constants $C,L,h_0>0$ such that, for $0<h\le h_0$:

1. for every exact solution $y(t)$ whose segment and the method states under consideration remain in a compact subset of $U$, the exact-start local defect satisfies $\|\Phi_h(y(t))-y(t+h)\|_2\le Ch^2$; and
2. for all $u,v\in U$, $\|\Phi_h(u)-\Phi_h(v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2$.

The defect is the method output minus the exact next state and the second inequality is one-step Lipschitz stability in the convention of [[def-one-step-ode-method-local-defect-order-and-stability]]. This result is restricted to a compact positive tube; it does not define the standard ratio formula at zero compartments.
thm-zero-compatible-modified-patankar-eu:
## Statement

Let a finite conservative PDS have a source-factored representation on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq\Omega$ of a compact set $K\subseteq[0,\infty)^m$, with factors that are $C^2$ on $U$ and nonnegative on $U\cap[0,\infty)^m$, as in [[def-source-factored-production-destruction-rates]]. For every $y^n\in K$ and $h>0$, [[alg-zero-compatible-modified-patankar-euler]] has a unique output $y^{n+1}\ge0$ and conserves $\sum_i y_i$. For the accuracy clause, fix a compact set $K_*\subset U$ containing $K$ and all exact solution segments under consideration, and define the smooth extension $\widetilde F_i(y):=\sum_{j\ne i}(y_j a_{ij}(y)-y_i a_{ji}(y))$ on $U$. If those exact segments remain in $K_*\cap[0,\infty)^m$, then the exact-start local defect is uniformly $O(h^2)$ as $h\downarrow0$, including when some coordinates of $y^n$ are zero. The claim is local; no global error bound at the boundary is asserted.
thm-mprk22-1-positive-conservative:
## Statement

For every finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]], every strictly positive input $y^n>0$, and every step size $h>0$, the stage and output of [[alg-mprk22-1]] are uniquely defined, strictly positive, and conserve total mass:

$$z>0,\qquad y^{n+1}>0,\qquad \sum_i z_i=\sum_i y_i^n=\sum_i y_i^{n+1}.$$

These preservation properties do not use the smoothness or compact-tube assumptions needed for the separate second-order error theorem.
lem-mprk22-1-positive-tube-local-error-a:
## Statement

Let $F$ be the vector field of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]] on a bounded open convex set $U\subset\Omega\cap\mathbb R_{>0}^m$ with $\overline U\subset\mathbb R_{>0}^m$. Assume the transfer rates are $C^2$ on an open neighborhood of $\overline U$, with derivatives through order two bounded there. Let $\Psi_h(y)$ be [[alg-mprk22-1]]. For sufficiently small $h>0$, there are constants $C,L,h_0>0$ such that:

1. for every exact solution segment in a compact subset of $U$, the exact-start defect satisfies $\|\Psi_h(y(t))-y(t+h)\|_2\le Ch^3$; and
2. for all $u,v\in U$, $\|\Psi_h(u)-\Psi_h(v)\|_2\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|_2$.

The local order-two estimate requires the positive lower bound on the stage denominators and the stated smoothness. Positivity and conservation for every $h>0$ are separate preservation properties and are not used to claim the local error order.
thm-modified-patankar-euler-global-first:
## Statement

Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, and $t_n=nh$. Let $y:[0,T]\to U$ solve the ODE of a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]], where the rates are $C^2$ on an open neighborhood in $\Omega$ of the compact positive tube $K\subset U$ of [[lem-modified-patankar-euler-positive-tube-local-error-and-stability]]. Let $y_0=y(0)$ and obtain $y_{n+1}$ by [[alg-modified-patankar-euler]] with $\sigma_i=(y_n)_i$. Suppose the exact path and every numerical state lie in the common compact tube $K$, and $h\le h_0$ for the local constants in that lemma. Then there is a constant $C_T$, independent of $N$, such that

$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_T h.$$

The conclusion is conditional on the stated positive compact tube; positivity and mass conservation alone do not establish that a trajectory remains in such a tube for a prescribed interval.
thm-patankar-inexact-solve-residual-ledg:
## Statement

Let $M\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}$ be an exact linear-system matrix from [[alg-modified-patankar-euler]] with admissible positive denominators, or from a stage/final solve of [[alg-mprk22-1]], for a finite conservative PDS. Let $b\ge0$ be its exact right-hand side. For either scheme, the PDS transfer identity gives $\mathbf 1^TM=\mathbf 1^T$ and strict column diagonal dominance, so $M^{-1}\ge0$. Let $\widehat y$ be a stored candidate and compute $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(M\widehat y)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-b)$ in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]], with $0<u<1$, $(m-1)u<1$, every nonzero exact intermediate normal, zero operations exact, successful sequential dot products and subtraction, and exact or certified upper bounds for the norms used by the supplier. Let $W$ be the certified allowance from [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]], using exact norms or certified upper bounds, and set $\rho:=\|\widehat w\|_2+W$. Then

$$\|M\widehat y-b\|_2\le\rho,\qquad \left|\mathbf1^T\widehat y-\mathbf1^Tb\right|\le\sqrt m\,\rho.$$

If $y^*:=M^{-1}b$ is the exact solution of the stored linear system, then

$$\|\widehat y-y^*\|_1\le\sqrt m\,\rho.$$

Consequently, the componentwise margin condition $\widehat y_i\ge\sqrt m\,\rho$ for every $i$ certifies $y^*\ge0$. A residual bound alone does not certify that the computed candidate $\widehat y$ is nonnegative. This certificate is relative to the stated stored matrix and right-hand side; any coefficient-assembly error relative to the intended real system must be separately bounded and added to the residual allowance.
thm-mprk22-1-global-second-order-error:
## Statement

Let $T>0$, $N\ge1$, $h=T/N$, and $t_n=nh$. Let $y:[0,T]\to U$ solve a finite conservative PDS [[def-finite-conservative-production-destruction-system]] whose transfer rates are $C^2$ on an open neighborhood in $\Omega$ of the compact positive tube $K\subset U$ in [[lem-mprk22-1-positive-tube-local-error-and-stability]]. Set $y_0=y(0)$ and compute each step with [[alg-mprk22-1]]. Suppose the exact solution, all numerical states, and every MPRK22(1) stage remain in the common compact tube $K$, and $h\le h_0$ for the local constants in that lemma. Then a constant $C_T$, independent of $N$, satisfies

$$\max_{0\le n\le N}\|y_n-y(t_n)\|_2\le C_T h^2.$$

This is a fixed-time, compact-tube convergence result; it does not assert a uniform error constant as the tube approaches a zero denominator or as stiffness parameters vary.
